_about: RED adversarial corpus — single source of truth (ARIA Part B / B1+B2+B4). Every entry is a vector that a defence must REFUSE. Each names its input, the expected refusal, the file:line of the defence, the finding that produced it, and a proof_catchable tag (B4): could a Lean theorem, in principle, have caught it? Most cannot — they live below the proof line, in the host, the channel, the parser boundary, the verifier. That tag is the Track-1/Track-2 boundary made concrete. Executable pins: js-validator entries run in test/red-corpus.test.cjs; the six-copy agreement runs in test/fleet-copy-differential.cjs, which is MANUAL and NOT run by CI (it needs all six repos side by side and the five siblings are private), so a green CI run on this repo says NOTHING about six-copy agreement; rust-host entries run in seal-host/rust/tests; verify-action entries run in seal-verify-action/test. Nothing here is a silent skip: an entry not executed by a given harness is printed as EXECUTED-ELSEWHERE with a pointer.

_schema.title: one line
_schema.finding: the finding / brief reference that produced this vector
_schema.capability: what the attacker must be able to do
_schema.surfaces: which refusing surfaces this fans to
_schema.vector: input + how to feed it (base fixture + mutation, or inline)
_schema.expected_refusal: what every listed surface must do
_schema.defence: repo:file:line of the check that must not silently disappear
_schema.executed_in: the harness file(s) that assert this

vectors.title: Receipt asserts its own trust via verifier-only field authority_trusted
vectors.finding: Monkey 2026-07-15 21:35 — kit validator 21 lines behind five downstream copies (T5 cross-copy differential, brief B2). Fail-OPEN leg: kit accepted what the five reject.
vectors.capability: Produce/relay a receipt object; inject a top-level authority_trusted field.

expected_refusal.error_substring: authority_trusted: verifier-computed only; forbidden in a receipt

proof_catchable.why: The hole is file duplication: six hand-maintained JS validator copies, one behind. No theorem about seal-host's Lean kernel can observe that a downstream JS receipt-format.js fell behind — the copies are below the proof line, in verifier code the proofs never mention.

vectors.title: KNOWN GAP (characterization, NOT a verified-consistent claim): kit producer omits signed_config; kit validator accepts what the five reject
vectors.finding: Monkey 2026-07-15 — copy-drift leg B. Fail-CLOSED: kit-produced mediated receipts bounce off stricter verifiers; no bad ALLOW. Deliberately NOT code-fixed pre-ARIA (fixing would require upgrading the kit signing path; risk > benefit for a fail-closed bug).
vectors.capability: None adversarial — this pins an intentional interop divergence so it cannot be mistaken for consistency.
surfaces: js-validator differential (kit accepts vs five reject)
vectors.defence: seal-check/receipt-format.js:353-365 (present in five); seal-assurance-kit/kernel/receipt-format.js intentionally omits — see the KNOWN GAP comment there.

proof_catchable.why: Producer/validator version skew across repos; a schema-version divergence in JS verifier code, invisible to any kernel theorem.

vectors.title: §11.1 unparseable receipt smuggling structured fields (tool/arguments) alongside a parse error
vectors.finding: serde/Lean divergence set (brief B2: 1e309, argless calls, non-object arguments). Option-B de-parse: when serde cannot re-parse a Lean-mediated line the receipt must omit tool/arguments/args_hash/canonical_*, carrying only request_sha256 + request_parse_error. A receipt that names a parse error AND carries structured fields is fabrication.
vectors.capability: Craft a line serde cannot re-parse but Lean mediates (e.g. numeric overflow 1e309); attempt to also present forged structured request fields.

expected_refusal.error_substring: must be absent on an unparseable-request receipt

vectors.defence: seal-check/receipt-format.js:246-261 (JS); seal-host/rust/src/decision_receipt.rs:205-237 (host omission); pinned in seal-host/rust/tests/differential.rs:195 (1e309 serde-vs-Lean).

proof_catchable.why: The serde re-parser and Lean's classifier are two different parsers of the same bytes. Lean's theorems cover what the KERNEL judged; the divergence is a property of the host's serde_json re-derivation, a layer the proofs deliberately do not model.

vectors.title: Legacy Schema K (seal_check_receipt) presented as a current receipt
vectors.finding: Hard-split ruling (seal-receipt-schema v1 day-2). A v0 seal-check receipt is NOT v1/v2-compatible and must be rejected, not silently coerced.
vectors.capability: Present an old-format receipt to a current verifier.

proof_catchable.why: Schema versioning is a verifier-layer discriminator; no kernel theorem exists about receipt wire-format versions.

vectors.title: Receipt with no recognized version discriminator
vectors.finding: Version-discriminator-first design (fail closed on unrecognized shape).
vectors.capability: Present an object lacking every known version key.

proof_catchable.why: Verifier-layer input validation; below the proof line.

vectors.title: Forge a pairing: kernel material from line A, request_sha256 from line B
vectors.finding: Brief B2 / red-team T2. The host cross-check and the verifiers must refuse a receipt whose kernel-attested request hash does not match the host's line hash.
vectors.capability: Compromised child / local user assembling a receipt from mismatched kernel output and request identity.

vector.description: Kernel audit request_sha256 for line A; host line hash for line B — mismatch. Also: a crafted line whose replayed hash occurs !=1 time to misfire the substitution count guard.

expected_refusal.detail: host returns Err (fails closed, nothing forwards); verifier requires the replayed hash to occur exactly once before substitution.

vectors.defence: seal-host/rust/src/decision_receipt.rs:135-145 (host cross-check, Err on mismatch); seal-assurance-kit/src/verify.cjs:134-140 (substitution-compare, split length===2 one-shot guard).
vectors.executed_in: Referenced-and-run: seal-host/rust/src/decision_receipt.rs::tests::forged_line_pairing_is_refused (host cross-check) + host_path.rs:784. The verifier substitution one-shot guard (verify.cjs:134-140) is DOCUMENTED here, not executably pinned this session — the load-bearing T2 defence is the host cross-check, which is pinned.

proof_catchable.why: The host cross-check (kernel-attested hash == host line hash) is a checkable Lean/host property. The SIX-copy verifier agreement on the substitution-compare is not — it lives in hand-maintained JS, below the proof line.

vectors.title: Terminator gap: "x\n" and "x\r\n" share a request commitment while the child receives different bytes
vectors.finding: Monkey read of the kernel-request-commitment plan / red-team T3. lean_view strips the terminator before Lean judges + before request_sha256; the child is forwarded the original bytes including terminator. Believed low impact (terminator not semantic) — pin the CURRENT behaviour honestly whichever way it is called.
vectors.capability: Send the same logical call with differing line terminators.

vector.description: sha256(lean_view("x\n")) == sha256(lean_view("x\r\n")) == sha256("x"); forwarded bytes differ.

expected_refusal.detail: commitment is over the terminator-stripped lean_view; forward carries original bytes. Honest name, no silent change.

proof_catchable.why: Lean's golden vector covers the commitment over the view Lean judged. The gap between 'what the kernel committed to' and 'what bytes were forwarded to the child' is a host transport property the kernel theorems do not reach.

vectors.title: Audit-stream injection via unknown_decision:<value> — quote-breaking, newline forging, ANSI smuggling
vectors.finding: Brief B2 / red-team T4. <=64 attacker-chosen chars reach stderr via unknown_decision:<value> on the unauthenticated control-file channel. Ben ruled keep-64 because json!() escaping at the emission site is the real control. Pin that the escaping holds under hostile input.
vectors.capability: Write an approval/control record with a decision value outside {absent,allow,deny}, containing quotes/newlines/ANSI/control bytes.

vector.description: decision value = '"}\n{"forged":"audit line"' and ANSI/control-byte variants; expect a single JSON-escaped warning line, record dropped, never approved.

expected_refusal.detail: record dropped (never approves); reason clamped to <=64 chars; emitted inside json!() so it cannot forge a second audit line.

vectors.defence: seal-host/rust/src/providers.rs:94-96 (<=64 clamp); seal-host/rust/src/main.rs approval_drop_line (json!() escaping at emission, called by emit_approval_drop_warnings).
vectors.executed_in: NEW: seal-host/rust/src/main.rs::tests::approval_drop_line_escapes_hostile_reason_no_second_audit_line (escaping) + seal-host/rust/src/providers.rs::tests::unknown_decision_reason_clamps_long_hostile_value_to_64_chars (clamp under long hostile value). Referenced-and-run: providers.rs::tests::{ed25519,control_file}_provider_drops_unknown_decision_never_approves (drop/never-approve).

proof_catchable.why: stderr audit-line escaping is a host/channel serialization property. Nothing the Lean kernel proves constrains how the Rust host renders a dropped-approval warning to a log stream.

vectors.title: Vacuous aggregate: [].every() is true — zero replay-applicable receipts must not claim consistency
vectors.finding: Brief B2 / already pinned in seal-verify-action; the pattern deserves a sweep. Every fleet aggregate that could be vacuously true is a candidate.
vectors.capability: Supply an evidence set with zero replay-applicable (or zero total) receipts.

vector.description: results=[] or replayApplicable=[]; a naive .every() would return true and claim signature/replay/authority consistency over nothing.

expected_refusal.detail: each aggregate ANDs a length>0 guard so an empty set yields false, never a spurious consistent verdict.

proof_catchable.why: Aggregate-over-empty-set semantics live in the verifier's JS. A theorem about a single receipt says nothing about how a fleet aggregator folds zero of them.
